resources.string: Lets you use the phone screen from the car: Mate replays the touches made on the car screen on the phone, and checks which app is in front so the phone screen stays paused while driving unless it shows a navigation app. Mate reads nothing else.
The phone screen is paused while the phone is locked. Unlock the phone to show it.

Turn on \u201cSound in the car\u201d in Mate on the phone, and choose Entire screen when Android asks: the phone screen uses the same permission.

The car wants to know which device is connected: with that it takes calls over its speakers and microphone, and some show a black screen otherwise. Mate reads the address itself where Shizuku allows it; otherwise it is under Settings > About phone > Status.

By default Mate uses the best codec the car and phone share (H.265…). Turn on if the car\'s picture is glitchy.

A paired wireless car is trusted on its first connection; a new USB or developer head unit only after you tap Trust (in its notification or on the home screen). Only trust a head unit you are connected to right now. If a head unit shows a different certificate later, you are asked again: only trust it if its software was updated.
Fine tuning for Google Maps, ABRP and others: an app\u2019s cards, lists and map content grow and shrink together.
One value for everything: bar, music, dashboard, navigation cards and foreign apps. Kept for %1$s; another car keeps its own size.

Head units check the phone\'s certificate. Open-source head units accept the generated one; cars using Google\'s head unit software only accept a certificate issued by Google, which Mate cannot include. You can import one you have the right to use (PEM certificate + PKCS#8 key, or PKCS#12), or download the one from the latest Android Auto app (from github.com/iscle/android-auto-certificates).
The certificate repository is gone (deleted or taken down): %1$s. Extract the certificate from the Android Auto app instead (see the README).
Couldn\'t download the certificate: %1$s. Check the connection and try again.
Like Android Auto\'s developer mode, for the desktop head unit, DHU, openauto, Headunit Revived. Reachable through adb only: adb forward tcp:5277 localabstract:aare_hu
Also listen on TCP port 5277 on every network, with no password. Anyone on the same Wi-Fi can connect and see the car screen and use the microphone.
Turn off network mode after a session
Safer: the network has to be allowed again for each session. Turn this off for head units that reconnect on their own, like openauto or Headunit Revived.
Also offer \"Phone screen\" to whoever connects here. Risky: they see the phone\'s screen and can tap on it, so leave it off unless you trust the head unit.
Accept a connection from an Android-Auto-in-the-browser app on this phone, for cars without Android Auto (e.g. Tesla). Any app on the phone could connect, so leave it off unless you use one.

Messages are read with the speech engine of this device. Voices that need the internet are computed by the engine\u2019s server and tend to sound better. Mate decides for each message: with Wi-Fi or good mobile reception the first voice below, else the second - one from the device, so nothing waits for a server.

Without internet or with poor reception
Loud tracks are turned down by what the Plex server measured (its loudness analysis). Applies from the next track.
Plex measures against \u221218 LUFS. Higher is louder; tracks quieter than the target stay as they are. Applies from the next track, for the other sources (switch below) at once.
Works on everything Mate sends to the car: its own music, audiobooks, other apps. Navigation prompts stay as they are.
Two layers: below, the measurement of your speakers; above, the sound preset. A preset never changes the measurement.
Evens out this car\'s speakers. Kept until you measure again. Choose here which measurement is used.
To compare, switch between the measurements – the music goes on.
Lies above the measurement. Per kind of app: music apps take the music preset, audiobook apps the audiobook preset.
Mate finds the kind of each app itself. Tap another kind if it is wrong.
·A = found by Mate. Navigation prompts always stay unfiltered.
Set the car\'s own equalizer to flat first. Raised bands lower the overall volume by the same amount, so nothing clips. Or let Mate measure the car below.
Applies to %1$s; every other car keeps its own sound.
Applies to the next car connected, and each one after until it gets its own values.

Mate plays about 20 seconds of test tones through the speakers: three times a gliding tone from lowest to highest, and listens with this device\'s microphone. How: 1. Parked only, doors and windows shut, fan off. 2. The car\'s equalizer and sound settings flat. 3. Volume at your usual level. 4. Hold the device at head height at the driver\'s seat, microphone free.

Reads messages and speaks the navigation. The voices on the device sound more natural than the phone\'s and need no network; Kokoro voices sound best. Mate computes the announcements ahead as soon as the route is set. Load once, then “Listen”.

Mate\'s speech recognition (Whisper, on the device) can be the voice input of every app: choose \"Mate speech recognition\" in the system settings.
Mate is new on this device. If you saved Mate\'s settings before (a ZIP from \"Transfer settings\"), they can be restored now: places, routes, views, sound and more.
Mate loads what it needs for its basic functions. Wi-Fi is best.
Microphone in the bar: a tap starts Mate\'s own voice control (Whisper, on the device); a long press opens the assistant chosen here.

Mate adapts to it: with an electric car the dashboard shows battery, range and charging, and the navigation plans charging stops with the level on arrival. With a combustion car Mate starts with the navigation, without battery tiles and charging stops.
Can be changed later under Settings → Dashboard.
For the car\'s data (battery, range, speed and more) Mate needs a Bluetooth OBD2 adapter in the car\'s diagnostic socket, or the IDmate server. Get an adapter that is known to work with your car.

Mind the compatibility: in modern cars the OBD socket has constant 12 V. An adapter that does not sleep can keep waking the car and drain the 12 V battery. Choose one with automatic sleep (or a switch) that is recommended for your model.
Calling in %1$d s – say \"cancel\" or tap X

Audio books, podcasts, other music apps and navigation prompts are measured on their way to the car and turned down to the same target level (never up). The first time this takes a few seconds per source, then Mate remembers it. Calls run over the hands-free connection of the car and stay as they are.
Bluetooth pairing with the car begun – please confirm it on the tablet.
The car\'s pairing code: %1$s – compare and confirm it on the tablet.
Fault marked – what is the problem?
Tap the microphone and say what is wrong.
Microphone: say more. Delete: say it anew.
I listen for as long as you like. Tap the microphone when you are done.
Still listening … (what you said is being worked out)
The last words are still being worked out …
The microphone or the speech recognition could not be had. Tap the microphone to try again.
The description is kept with the fault.
Something is still missing for voice control and announcements on the device. Load it now? Best on Wi-Fi.
When a call comes in, Mate rings in the car until you answer or decline. A tap plays the tone briefly.
The car\'s Wi-Fi is made known to the tablet as a normal network. Where it has internet, the tablet uses it instead of mobile data. Android asks once whether Mate may suggest networks.
The car\'s Wi-Fi wants a login: tap \"Sign in to network\" on the tablet. Until then the internet goes over mobile data.
The car is no longer parked – the app is closed and paused.
The issue log leaves out positions, places, names, networks, addresses and tokens, for a public bug report. Have a look before posting it.

Play the sounds one after another, music may play. Each goes over the navigation channel like a prompt. If you hear crackle, tap “Crackle heard” right after, else “Sound clean” – it goes into the log with the channel’s figures.
Test sentence in the navigation voice
In 300 metres turn right onto Main Street, then after 1 kilometre keep left.
Open Mate Navi once, then the voice speaks here.
How Mate brings the music back after a prompt. The choice stays for the drives after. With music playing tap “Test prompt”, then say whether the music came back up.
As before: ask for the music at once
Give the prompt up first, music 0.3 s later
Open the music’s stream to the car anew
Ask for the music again after 1.5 s
Keep Mate from being slowed down
Android slows Mate down when the screen is off – the sound to the car may then crackle. Allow Mate to run without battery optimisation.
Tone in 15 s (switch the screen off meanwhile)
The cinema is switched off. Switch it on in the Mate app under Settings → Apps → Cinema.
No app chosen for the cinema yet. Choose them in the Mate app under Settings → Apps → Cinema.
Shizuku runs but has not allowed Mate yet. Open the Mate app on the tablet and allow Shizuku.
Shizuku is not started. After every restart of the tablet tap “Start” in the Shizuku app.
The cinema needs Shizuku. Install Shizuku on the tablet and start it.
Calling in during the call with %1$s
Mate is a fork of AARE (github.com/prototux/AARE) and, like AARE, licensed under the GPL-3.0-or-later; source: github.com/TheInGoF/AARE-Mate. These parts keep their own licence:
Pair once: in the developer options turn on \"Wireless debugging\" and open \"Pair device with pairing code\". Then type the code here, keeping that window open.
Pairing found. Type the six-digit code here.
No pairing found yet. Please open \"Pair device with pairing code\" and type the code again.
Pairing did not work. Check the code and type it again.
Paired. From now on Mate starts Shizuku itself when it is not running (when the car connects, after a restart, when the app opens). The tablet needs a Wi-Fi network for it.
Paired, but Shizuku could not be started just now. The reason is in the diagnostic log (\"shizuku by Mate\").
Shizuku is not running. Mate starts it itself as soon as there is Wi-Fi; tap to try now.
Shizuku is not running. Tap: pair Mate once with wireless debugging, then Mate starts Shizuku itself - also after every restart.
Trips and charges, seen on the tablet
A trip starts as soon as the car leaves P and ends once it has stood in P this long. Distance and route come from the car\'s GPS, battery level and charging from the telemetry stick.
A trip ends after … in P
Connect the stick: Settings → Dashboard → \"Connect the dashboard\" → Telemetry stick → \"Find stick\". Without the stick, battery level, consumption and charges are missing.
No trip yet. They appear after the first trip with the car connected.
Found from the battery level (the car was not connected while charging).
End not seen: the car was switched off while charging.
